data.description:
`_deprecations.py` is a typed tombstone registry: each retired input records whether encountering
it should warn or hard-error. Two of the three kinds are wired — `raise_or_warn_env`
(`config.py:389,391`) and `raise_or_warn_cfg_key` (`_config_schema.py:37,766`).

The third is not. `raise_or_warn_file` (`_deprecations.py:290`) has ZERO callers anywhere,
including tests. Instead `config.py:392-394` hand-rolls the raise for the single registered file
tombstone, ignoring the row's `behavior` field entirely.

This is currently invisible because the one registered file entry (`.rebar/config.conf`,
`_deprecations.py:228`) carries behavior `error` and the hand-rolled code raises — so the bypass
and the registry agree by coincidence. It breaks the moment a file entry is added with behavior
`warn`, or the existing one is downgraded: the registry would say one thing and the code do another.

`docs/config.md` promises the `error` class "raises a targeted migration error and exits
non-zero". Today that promise holds only by that coincidence, and only `rebar config validate`
reports file tombstones at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `config.py` calls `raise_or_warn_file` instead of hand-rolling the raise
- [ ] The registry row's `behavior` field decides the outcome
- [ ] A test covers a `warn`-class file tombstone, which today has no coverage
data.title: Honour the deprecation registry's behavior field for file tombstones
